title: Multiple Bodies
text: Dimensional Kerberos had appeared there too, I say. Not just one—how many of them were there, I wondered!? Soldiers and adventurers were getting wounded while trying to protect the civilians. …Since their attention had drifted toward the voices and away from me, I seized the moment, used Cloaking Lance and Fire Mirage to vanish from sight, leapt up to a high vantage point, and—
“Gungnir X!”

With a stan! I pierced a Dimensional Kerberos from the shadow of a building, finishing it off in a single blow. Following up, I locked onto multiple Dimensional Skeletons with Aiming Lancer, taking care not to hit any people as I unleashed it.
“Aiming Lancer X!”

Statatatan! A rain of spears poured down upon the monster-besieged town, piercing through the creatures one after another. The spears weren’t especially well-suited against skeletons, but the sheer force of each blow sent them flying regardless.
“What is this attack!?”
“It’s like that rain of destruction that sank the ships one after another!?”
“Where is it coming from!?”

Since I’d managed to conceal myself well while attacking, the people of Éclair’s parents’ town didn’t immediately realize I was the culprit and instead looked around in confusion. I figured I’d thinned their numbers quite a bit by now. While I was at it, I struck at the wave’s rift too, but it seemed the condition for closing it hadn’t been met—probably because not all the boss Kerberos had been dealt with yet, since it refused to close.
I never imagined there’d be multiple of them spawning. Somebody should’ve told me, I say! That there were several!

That was what I thought, but… it seemed the flame sac had caught fire, because the Dimensional Kerberos I’d just finished off began blazing furiously. That fire was intense. It burned so thoroughly that not even bones remained, as if it held the very flames of hell within it. Being someone skilled in fire magic myself, I could tell. Was it trying to say that if I didn’t swiftly deal with the flame sac, the corpse itself would burn away? Perhaps Éclair’s parents had finished one off, and the Melromarc knights who arrived later only saw the one that was left behind? How thoroughly troublesome, I say.

In any case, treating it as a simple matter of extinguishing a fire, I used a flame-dousing spell to put out the blaze consuming the Dimensional Kerberos. I hoped someone would secure the materials later and turn them into equipment.
“In any case, everyone! We protect the people from the monsters’ advance, no matter what!”
“Ohhh!”
“…That we reinforced our defenses out of caution against some mysterious threat, only for it to turn out this way—what a strange stroke of fortune… no, wait.”

Éclair’s parent’s expression turned thoughtful at that. Hmm… quite sharp, it seemed. I’d only heard secondhand, but there was no doubt this one was a capable subordinate of the Queen. By all accounts, a reliable figure in peacetime, more so than Trash ever was—losing someone like that in the very first wave would’ve been a real blow. Compared to Éclair, the gap in intelligence and charisma was like night and day. To put it plainly, Éclair doesn’t have much of either charisma or wit. Elephant was a strictly superior upgrade in every sense, I say. Come to think of it, perhaps that evil god lurking as the Crimson Swine’s true body had been deliberately targeting and killing the very people whose loss would be most devastating. But not this time, I say! Not this timmmmme!

In any case, I’d whittled down the threatening monsters advancing on the town considerably. Surely there was no more danger of a crisis at this point? Still, the chaos of battle hadn’t let up. Staying within the bounds of not being noticed, I went searching for more Dimensional Kerberos, aiming to end the wave swiftly. Most likely, if I finished off the one that had headed toward the village, the wave would end. Éclair’s parent and Crocodile Guy’s parent should be fine for a while yet. Statatan! Off I ran, dashing toward the village!
And so, having made my way to Big Sister’s village to check on the situation…
“Drifa Chain Lightning!”
With a crackle of bachibachi, Older Sister unleashed a lightning spell at a Dimensional Kerberos, then followed it up by hurling a lightning-wreathed harpoon.
“Thunderstrike Harpoon!”
“Gah—gaaah—”

The Dimensional Kerberos seemed to recognize Older Sister as the greatest threat present, trying to dodge the lightning magic and close the distance, only to be sent reeling back by the follow-up harpoon strike. Truly, quite the formidable fighter. Though there were wounded, it looked like no one had died. The adults had formed up in a protective formation around the children—Big Sister, her friends, and Keel among them. Thanks to the fishermen being in the village, they’d managed to hold their ground.
“‘Source of power, by my command—light, slay the enemy before me!’”
“Fast Holy!”
Oh? The person who appeared to be Big Sister’s father unleashed a light spell in support. Quite the powerful one, wasn’t it?
“Buuuuu!”

Meanwhile, a pig who closely resembled Big Sister—probably a parent—swung a cleaver down, crushing the skull of an approaching Dimensional Skeleton. Its fighting style bore an odd resemblance to Big Sister’s own. Not quite on Older Sister’s level, but undoubtedly a skilled fighter in its own right.
“Sadeena!”
“Yeah!”

Thanks to Older Sister’s group coordinating well, the Dimensional Kerberos was already badly wounded—it looked like finishing it off was just a matter of time even without further interference. Still, that didn’t mean I was about to just stand by and watch. If I took down that Dimensional Kerberos, it would probably satisfy the condition for ending the wave. So—time for a long-range sniping Gungnir, I say!
“Gungnir X!”
I hurled my spear with all my strength, piercing straight through the Dimensional Kerberos that Older Sister and the others were fighting.
“Gyaaan—!?”
A single sudden, flawlessly accurate spear strike was all it took to finish off the Dimensional Kerberos.
“Oh?”
“Wh-what was that!? Where did that attack come from!?”

The man who appeared to be Big Sister’s father narrowed his eyes, having noticed roughly where I’d thrown from. This was dangerously close to being spotted, so I layered concealment spell after concealment spell, hid in the shadow of a building, and dashed toward the rift.
“This world has no need for tragedy, I say!”

Praying that I’d managed to avert whatever tragedy might have befallen Big Sister and the others, I hurled my spear into the wave’s rift and sealed it shut! The color of the sky swiftly returned to its original blue. All that remained now was to mop up the scattered Dimensional Skeletons, and the damage should be kept to a minimum. Checking on the state of the village… the Dimensional Kerberos had apparently rampaged about quite a bit, leaving some scorch marks here and there, but overall the damage fell short of anything truly severe.
“The sky…”
“It’s blue again…”
“Is it… over?”
The villagers, along with the people from the wave-affected region, all gazed up at the sky.
“Everyone! Don’t let your guard down! There are still monsters about!”
“Yeah! Let’s do this!”
“Bubuu!”
Keel and Keel’s parent struck a pose.
“Bubububu, bubu!”
Keel, apparently deciding it was safe now, called out something to the parent once more.
“Is it over?”

Big Sister and her friends, who had been trembling, seemed to sense the shift in mood and dashed over to embrace their visibly relieved parents. Older Sister, too, let out a sigh of relief, resting the harpoon on her shoulder with a smile.
“No idea. Next thing I knew, Sadeena here was waking me up.”
As Keel’s parent said this, the attention of the villagers all turned toward Older Sister.
“…Big Sister just happened to be exploring the area a bit and found you, that’s all. Never in my wildest dreams did I imagine something like this would happen.”
“If Sadeena and the others hadn’t been here, I dread to think what might’ve happened to the monsters—or rather, what might’ve happened to us, if we’d been out fishing at the time.”
Big Sister’s father—the one who’d been searching for me—murmured this with an expression of relief directed at Older Sister.
“The sea looks awfully rough too. I wonder what it’s like further out…”

Hmm… there was no doubt this was an unusually wide-reaching wave. Looking at the sea, it was more turbulent than I’d ever seen it. Now that I thought of it… I recalled hearing about just how rough the sea could get. Apparently, the damage had reached places far, far away. At the time, a considerable number of ships and residents out at sea had reportedly lost their lives. Even in my memories of the world I originally came from, there were tales of disasters whose effects had reached surprisingly far—something along those lines, I say.
